instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Independent film and TV production company developing and producing scripted drama series and feature documentaries for streaming platforms and broadcasters. Vertex Group maintains a slate of 6 projects in various stages of development, focusing heavily on optimizing content acquisition and distribution efficiency. We operate across multiple international locations and have distinct functional leadership spanning operations, commercial strategy, finance, and technology.
answers.pastInitiatives: We piloted a cloud-based project management tool last year to streamline internal workflows, but adoption was inconsistent across teams, leading us to revert to spreadsheets for core tracking. This experience highlighted that innovation in our environment requires more structured change management and incentive alignment than our informal process currently provides.
answers.strategicGoals: We are heavily dependent on a single product category (content production) and a concentrated customer base; thus, this concentration risk is unacceptable for long-term health. Our primary goal is to identify and develop new revenue streams, possibly including licensing intellectual property or launching niche spin-off content lines that leverage our existing production infrastructure.
answers.additionalContext: Vertex Group faces increasing competition from major streamers and a growing demand for interactive media experiences. While our production quality is high, scaling new content types requires significant investment in emerging technologies.
answers.teamSize: The technology organization is structured into product-aligned squads with a central platform team of 5 engineers enabling shared infrastructure. Innovation is driven by a '20% time' policy where all engineers can dedicate one day per sprint to self-directed projects, plus a quarterly internal pitch competition where winning ideas receive seed funding and 3 months of dedicated squad allocation.

opportunities.title: AI-Driven Script Coverage and Sentiment Scoring
opportunities.rationale: Leveraging AI tools to rapidly analyze script coverage against emerging market trends can accelerate greenlight decisions without requiring a complete overhaul of production infrastructure. This incremental step improves operational efficiency immediately.

first_actions: Pilot an existing generative AI tool on 2 current projects
Establish a dedicated 'Content Intelligence' working group within the tech squad
resources_needed: Subscription fees for specialized script analytics software ($5k)
Time allocation from 1 senior engineer per quarter (internal resource)
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction of project greenlight cycle time by 10%
milestones: Q4: Successful pilot execution on two projects

opportunities.title: IP Licensing and Consulting Division
opportunities.rationale: To achieve diversification, Vertex Group could launch a new business model focusing on monetizing its established IP (e.g., character rights, production methodologies) through licensing or high-level content consulting services. This moves beyond media production into intellectual property management.

first_actions: Conduct an internal market feasibility study on secondary revenue streams
Develop a core 'IP Readiness' service offering pitch deck
resources_needed: Legal consultation fees for IP framework ($10k)
Allocation of 2 dedicated business development hours per week
execution_plan.success_metric: Secure first consulting contract worth $50k within 1 year
milestones: Q4: Launch pilot licensing partnership agreement

next_steps.action: Formalize a 3-year diversification roadmap with clear KPIs for new revenue streams.
Mandate structured cross-functional workshops to address the 'culture' barrier surrounding radical ideas.

key_weaknesses: Inconsistent technology adoption and lack of standardized change management protocols for new tools.
Weak alignment between informal innovation efforts ('20% time') and long-term strategic diversification goals.
Scarcity of specialized creative and technical talent required to pursue radical, non-core ventures.
Centralized decision-making structure that may bottleneck the small leadership team during high-velocity innovation cycles.
